metaDescription: Latest conference talks, appointments, publications and lab milestones from Candice P. Chu, DVM, PhD, DACVP at Texas A&M University.
intro: Updates on conferences, appointments, publications, and lab activities.
_note: Newest first. iso = sort key (YYYY-MM-DD); date = displayed string (MMM DD, YYYY).

items.html: 👩‍🏫 Upcoming: Dr. Chu teaches the afternoon session on vibe-coding tools at the AI Jumpstart Bootcamp, run by the Texas A&M Institute of Data Science with High Performance Research Computing.

📝 Publication: PhD student Yumi Chang's first paper, Applying artificial intelligence to automate clinical data extraction from veterinary electronic health records, is out in the Veterinary Pathology special issue on artificial intelligence — open access.
🎤 Invited talk: Less pAIn, More gAIn: A Starter Guide to AI Literacy for Veterinary Professionals at the AVMA Convention 2026 in Anaheim, hosted by IDEXX.

✈️ Workshop: Dr. Chu and Dr. Mary Nabity delivered a two-day workshop on cytology, urinalysis and renal biomarkers for the Taiwan Academy of Veterinary Internal Medicine, attended by more than 200 veterinarians.
🎤 Presentation: PhD student Yumi Chang gave an oral presentation at the ACVIM Forum on extracting clinical data from medical records, in collaboration with VetRec and the Dog Aging Project.
📚 Textbook: Dr. Chu contributed to an AI literacy textbook for veterinary medicine, to be published by Springer Nature.

📝 Publication: Computer Vision and Deep Learning in Small Animal Cytology and Slide Review — an invited review in Veterinary Clinics of North America: Small Animal Practice covering computer vision fundamentals, publication guidelines, and how nine veterinary organizations address AI in their position statements.
📣 Recruiting: The lab is offering fully funded, salaried two-year MS-thesis positions for DVM students interested in applying AI to veterinary medicine. See Team for how to apply.
📝 Publication: Curriculum framework for artificial intelligence literacy in veterinary education is out in Frontiers in Veterinary Science, with PhD student Avery Huang as first author.
✈️ Conference: Dr. Chu is heading to the Purina Institute Global Summit 2025 to present "The impact of AI on veterinary diagnostics and consulting."
🎉 Dr. Chu has been appointed to join the Association of American Veterinary Medical Colleges AI Working Group to advance veterinary medicine!
✈️ Conference: Dr. Chu is heading to the VMX 2025 Veterinary Conference to teach hematology and talk about AI.
👩‍🏫 Workshop: Dr. Chu is hosting Data Science for Veterinary Researchers with Texas A&M Institute of Data Science on Feb 17–21, 2025.
🎉 Dr. Chu has been appointed to join the AVMA Task Force on Emerging Technologies and Innovation!
🖥️ Video: Watch Dr. Chu's Research Conversation Series talk How I Streamline Academic Writing with AI and Digital Tools on YouTube.
🔈 Podcast: Listen to The A.C.V.P. Podcast for A Conversation with Dr. Candice Chu on Spotify or Apple Podcasts.
📝 Article: Dr. Chu has published Banish the PDF-hunting blues with these AI and digital tools in Nature Career column.
🌐 On-demand webinar: How I Streamline Academic Writing with AI and Digital Tools (ACVIM) — free to ACVIM candidates and diplomates.
📝 Article: Canine Round Cell Tumor Cytology published in Vet Focus.
📺 Media coverage: Texas A&M Researcher Explores Benefits Of AI In Veterinary Medicine, Education — Texas A&M Today.
🎉 Dr. Chu is officially back to Aggieland to establish the Chu Lab!
🌐 On-demand webinar: All you Need to Know About Round Cell Tumor Cytology — VETgirl ($50.00).
🎉 Chu Lab welcomes first graduate student — Dr. Yumi Chang!
📝 Article: Top 3 Conditions Missed by Skipping Urinalysis — Clinician's Brief.
🖥️ Video: I AM CVM — Dr. Candice Chu (VMBS Facebook).
📺 Media coverage: CVM Brings Home Top Awards from Annual Pathology Meeting — VMBS News.
📺 Media coverage: CVM Students Win Awards at ACVP Annual Meeting — VMBS News.

_source: Items July 2026 and earlier in 2026 were compiled from Dr. Chu's own LinkedIn activity export (July 2026). Dates are the event dates stated in each post; where a post gave only a month, the display date is month-precision and the iso value is used for sorting only.
